i0: Good English avoids **repeating** words. We can **leave words out** (*ellipsis*): *I wanted to go, but I couldn't (go).* Or we can **replace** them with a short word (*substitution*): *I don't like this shirt. Can I see a different **one**?*
i1: For short answers and *so do I*, see [So Do I, Neither Do I](/blog/grammar/so-do-i-neither-do-i/). For *I think so*, see the same page.
ell-one.t: One and ones: the red one, these ones
ell-one.s: Use ***one*** (singular) and ***ones*** (plural) instead of repeating a **countable noun**: *I don't like this jacket. I prefer the black **one**. These shoes are nicer than the old **ones**.*
ell-one.b0.1.1: *My phone is broken. I need a new **one**.*
ell-one.b0.2.1: *The **one** on the left is mine. The **ones** I bought were cheap.*
ell-one.b1: Don't use *one* for **uncountable** nouns: *I like white wine more than red* (not *red one*).
ell-one.b2: After *this / that*, *one* is often used: *I'll take **this one***. After *these / those*, *ones* is optional in BrE: *I prefer **those (ones)**.*
